## What it is

qBittorrent downloads and shares files over BitTorrent. This package runs `qbittorrent-nox`, the version without a desktop window, and you use it through its web interface ([qbittorrent/qBittorrent](https://github.com/qbittorrent/qBittorrent)).

**Licence:** `GPL-3.0-or-later`. From `COPYING` at release-5.3.0: the source is GPLv2 or later, and "the binary distribution is licensed under ... GPLv3 or ... any later version" because it contains GPLv3+ assets. Both add a permission to link with OpenSSL; SPDX has no identifier for that exception, so the manifest names the base licence only. GitHub reports `NOASSERTION`, so the licence gate relies on the license-matrix row "qBittorrent". Market class **L2**. The image comes from qBittorrent's own `qbittorrent/docker-qbittorrent-nox` repo (GPL-3.0).

**Legal notice (upstream text):** "qBittorrent is a file sharing program. When you run a torrent, its data will be made available to others by means of upload. Any content you share is your sole responsibility." OneMind does not confirm this notice for you (`QBT_LEGAL_NOTICE` is unset), so qBittorrent prints it to its log on every start.

**Icon:** a neutral generated icon with initials; no upstream logo is shipped.

## Market listing

- Category and sub-tags (docs/design/TAXONOMY.md §1): media: downloads. The sub-tags go into `metadata.tags` once the schema has it.
- Deployment class (TAXONOMY §2): **Market · community** until CI writes a passing scan (contract §9.4), then Market · verified if every check passes.

## How it runs here

- One `Deployment` (`Recreate`), one container, as `qbtUser` (UID 1000, the image's own user). The entrypoint skips its root-only steps (PUID/PGID) when started non-root. Read-only root filesystem with a `/tmp` scratch volume, as upstream's `--read-only` example; no privilege escalation, all capabilities dropped.
- Volumes: `qbittorrent-config` (1 GiB, `/config`) and `qbittorrent-downloads` (100 GiB, `/downloads`, the default save path).
- Probes: `GET /` on the WebUI port 8080.
- Stop grace period 30 minutes, as upstream asks, so resume data is written before the pod stops.

## First run

Source: [docker-qbittorrent-nox Readme](https://github.com/qbittorrent/docker-qbittorrent-nox#readme).

1. Install qBittorrent from the Market and approve the action. It installs into `app-qbittorrent`.
2. Read the temporary WebUI password from the log (qBittorrent 4.6.1 and later print one on first start):
   ```sh
   kubectl -n app-qbittorrent logs deploy/qbittorrent | grep -i password
   ```
3. Forward the port and open http://localhost:8080, then sign in as `admin` with that password:
   ```sh
   kubectl -n app-qbittorrent port-forward svc/qbittorrent 8080:8080
   ```
4. In Options, Web UI, set your own password right away (the temporary one changes on every restart until you do).

## Not done yet

- **Incoming connections:** the torrent port 6881 is not reachable from outside the box (OneMind apps cannot use host ports yet), so other peers cannot connect in. Downloads still work through outgoing connections, usually more slowly.
- No VPN option. Traffic leaves through the box's normal internet connection.
- No HTTPS or LAN hostname: OneMind v0 has no ingress or certificates for apps, so the web UI is reached through a port-forward until the app proxy exists.
- Resource figures are OneMind choices; upstream publishes none. They are checked against real use when the CI smoke test (contract §9.4 check 9) runs.
- `metadata.tier` stays `community` until `sdk/tools/app-gate` in CI writes a passing `scan.json`. `spec.updates.automerge` is `none` until `renovate.json` lists the app.

## Why this app is blocked

The CI app gate (`sdk/tools/app-gate`, contract §9.4) computed tier **blocked** for this app on 2026-11-12 (ci-apps run 43212771377, job `gate (qbittorrent)`). The gateway lists a blocked app in the Market but refuses to install it (§10.3, §11.1). The app is kept, not hidden, and the gate was not weakened. Reasons from that run:

- Vulnerability: `docker.io/qbittorrentofficial/qbittorrent-nox:5.3.0-2`: CVE-2026-111497 in `brotli-libs` 1.2.0-r1, fixed in 1.2.1-r0.
- Smoke test failed: `GET /` on Service `qbittorrent:8080` returned 401 (the web UI wants a login; the gate accepts 2xx and 3xx). The process is up. Whether a different smoke path or setting is right needs a look at the app's first-run behaviour.
- Passed: licence (matrix row for qBittorrent matches), ClamAV (0 infected).

To unblock: move the image pin to a release that fixes the CVE (tag verified with `crane`), and make the smoke test pass (for example by having the manifest start the web UI without an auth wall on `/`, if upstream supports it safely; do not weaken the login). Then rerun `sdk/tools/app-gate`.
